rewriters.name: nullOnDivZero
rewriters.note: NOT a ≃ₑ rewriter: used only by the strict check of the duckdb dialect (checkQuery, registry row 23) so that a division or modulo by zero is not counted as an error. Contract: every other error still surfaces (a divisor that errors or is not a number, and a dividend that errors or is not a number: the zero arm is NULL = (a op 1), the operator's own type check of the dividend; since 25 Nov 2026, when NULL = a still hid name / 0). Audit it against that contract, not against ≃ₑ; it must never feed a result or a rewriter

rewriters.name: SqlBridge.Inline.query
rewriters.note: NOT a ≃ rewriter: inlines non-recursive CTEs as derived tables before elaboration (phase 9.2, #460). Contract: every table reference whose folded name a CTE binds is replaced by its body, everywhere a table can occur (FROM, joins, derived tables, subqueries in any expression, window arguments); a CTE sees only the earlier ones; a body naming its own CTE reads the base table; a WITH nested inside returns none. Sound because SQL fixes no evaluation strategy for a non-recursive CTE and no SQL function in the fragment is volatile. Checked against DuckDB and Postgres by BridgeDiffTest's WITH cases; audit it against that contract, not against an equivalence relation

rewriters.name: SqlBridge.bindView
rewriters.note: NOT a ≃ rewriter: substitutes a recursive CTE's elaborated query for its table while elaborating WITH RECURSIVE (phase 9.6, #464; Query.recurse reads the working table through outer). Contract: every arm of Query, including outerJoin, window and recurse, is traversed, and only references to the CTE's table are replaced. A missing arm drops the substitution silently (one was missed for outerJoin and fixed before #488), so check every Query constructor has an arm. Checked by RecurseExamples (kernel) and BridgeDiffTest's WITH RECURSIVE cases against DuckDB and Postgres

rewriters.name: SqlEquiv.effectiveHaving
rewriters.proof: none (by design; it defines the oracle's semantics)
rewriters.note: NOT a ≃ rewriter: the reference oracle evaluates a query whose only aggregate is in ORDER BY (orderByOnlyAggregates: no GROUP BY, no HAVING, no aggregate in the items, windows included) with HAVING TRUE, so it is one group, as DuckDB and Postgres do (#445, registry row 22; the sqlite dialect rejects it at parse time). Contract: it changes nothing else (effectiveHaving_of_not, _some, _nil, _cases); evalSelectCore, evalSelectAfterFilter and Strict's checkSelect all apply it, and must stay in step. Theorems that rule out an implicit group carry orderByOnlyAggregates … = false or are stated over effectiveHaving. Checked by SemanticsTest order_by_aggregate_only_* and the DiffDuckdb/DiffPostgres 'implicit group:' cases

relation.name: ExprEquiv (≃ₑ)
relation.equality: Lean propositional equality on Option Value: kind-strict (distinct Value constructors never coincide); rewrite patterns match constructors, so host-language equality confusion cannot arise
weakerVariantsToReject: ExprEquivEmptyDb (≃ₑ₀): empty database only. Known, correctly labelled users: decideGroundExprEquivInst and decideGroundExprEquiv_sound decide ≃ₑ₀ for ground expressions and must not be used to conclude ≃ₑ
typedCoreRelations: SqlCore.Expr.Equiv Γ: equal results on every row conforming to Γ (typed core; conformance is part of the typed semantics, not a gap)
SqlCore.Query.Equiv ℓ: on every conforming database instance, at level ℓ (.ordered, bags, sets)

probe.note: The LSpec probe exercises SqlEquiv's expression rewriters only; the SqlCore simplifier and checkers rely on their kernel-checked proofs and the decide +kernel tests in SqlCore/Check.lean

trustGuard: Test/TrustBaseTest.lean (SqlEquiv); SqlCoreTest/TrustBaseTest.lean (#assert_trust_base SqlCore and SqlBridge; scripts/lean/check_trust_base.sh cannot import SqlBridge, which has no root module)
projectSpecificChecks: checkEquivFull may conclude ≃ₑ from ground evaluation only when both sides are Expr.isClosed; Expr.isGround admits database-dependent EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t)
Dialect operators (BinOp.likeCI, MIN/MAX modes) must not be matched by rewrite arms whose proofs cover only the default operator
When a Value constructor is added, the LSpec generators and tools/definition_coverage_matrix.py must learn it in the same PR (CLAUDE.md)

No partial def, unsafe, implemented_by, extern or native_decide may be reachable from the evaluator, a rewriter, a tactic or a checker (#278); the remaining partial defs (66 on 23 Nov 2026: 48 Parser, 8 Pretty, 10 toReprStr; count with grep -rnE "^\s*(private |protected )?partial def" SqlEquiv/, since a plain grep also matches comments) are only in Parser.lean, Pretty.lean and toReprStr. Test/TrustBaseTest.lean (#assert_no_runtime_overrides) and Test/TacticTest.lean (#guard_msgs on axioms) enforce this. In SqlCore/ and SqlBridge/ the only partial defs allowed are the Spider coverage reporter (SqlBridge/Coverage.lean, 9 on 23 Nov 2026), off every proof and checker path: grep -rnE "^\s*(private |protected )?partial def" SqlCore/ SqlBridge/
No theorem may have textually identical sides (it would prove nothing; #307): tools/rewrite-audit/scripts/lean/find_identical_sides.py SqlEquiv SqlCore SqlBridge must report OK. CI runs it
The LSpec probe exercises only expression rewriters; statement checkers (checkSelectEquiv, checkQueryEquiv) rely on their kernel-checked proofs and the smoke tests in StatementChecker.lean
